title: Kestrel and the Veil
premise: Paloma Ashgrove, a scribe indentured to the Ledger Guild of Vess, discovers that the guild's 'impossible things' are fragments of a country called Kestrel that was erased from the world two centuries ago — and that the child at his door, speaking its dead tongue, is the last living citizen. The ledgers Paloma keeps are actually the country's remaining borders, and the Guild has been selling them off piece by piece to buyers who want erased power. To save the child and himself, Paloma must reconstruct Kestrel's true name from scattered ledger pages, open the door out of a nation that no longer exists, and pay the inheritance price: someone must remember Kestrel completely, forever, in exchange for the child's freedom. In the end Paloma chooses to become the country's sole memory, trading his own history for the boy's future, and walks out of the world carrying a nation inside him.
about_author: Kestrel Montrose is the pen name of a former archivist who spent seven years cataloguing the property records of dissolved nations before turning to fiction. They write from a house built on the site of a tollgate no map remembers.

chapters.title: The Weight of Ink
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. We meet him mid-audit, cataloguing impossible inventory — bottled thunder, a widow's second shadow — while calculating how many years remain on his debt. The emotional beat is weary competence masking quiet desperation; he believes ledgers are safer than lives.

chapters.title: A Knock in the Old Tongue
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. A mud-caked boy arrives at the guild's night door speaking a language no scribe can parse — except the oldest ledger answers him, pages stirring on their own. The beat is uncanny wonder colliding with institutional fear.

chapters.title: Inventory of Ghosts
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Hiding the boy in the archive, Paloma cross-references the language against sealed folios and finds entries for a country called Kestrel, struck through but not deleted. The beat is the thrill of forbidden discovery curdling into dread.

chapters.title: The Guildmaster's Smile
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Guildmaster Corvane summons him, reveals she knows about the boy, and offers a bargain: deliver the child to a buyer, and Paloma's debt dissolves. The beat is temptation sharpened by menace.

chapters.title: What the Boy Remembers
chapters.summary: Alternating POV between Paloma and the boy, Tam. Through broken translation, Tam describes streets, festivals, a mother — memories of a place that never existed. The beat is grief for something neither of them ever had.

chapters.title: Buyers and Borders
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. He tails Corvane to an auction where nobles bid on 'provenance shards' — literal pieces of Kestrel's geography. The beat is horror: the country wasn't destroyed, it was dismembered and sold.

chapters.title: Running the Ledger
chapters.summary: Tam's POV. Tam steals a shard and drags Paloma into flight through Vess's undercity; wherever the shard goes, phantom streets briefly overlay real ones. The beat is exhilarating escape shadowed by Tam's homesickness.

chapters.title: The Cartographer's Debt
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. They seek Sefa Ilun, a disgraced cartographer who once mapped Kestrel before its erasure; she agrees to help only if Paloma signs over his one possession — his mother's ring. The beat is sacrifice as down payment.

chapters.title: Pages That Bleed
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. Reconstructing the true-name manuscript, they learn each recovered page costs the reader a memory. Sefa has already forgotten her daughter's face. The beat is the theme made explicit: remembering has a price.

chapters.title: Corvane's Hand
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Guild enforcers raid Sefa's shop; Sefa burns her life's maps to cover their escape and is taken. The beat is guilt — Paloma survives because others pay.

chapters.title: The Erasure War
chapters.summary: Tam's POV, dream-vision. Tam relives Kestrel's final night: its people chose erasure over conquest, scattering themselves into objects and orphans. The beat is tragic understanding — Tam is a refugee from a suicide.

chapters.title: Half a Name
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. With most pages gathered, the door out of Kestrel remains locked: the name requires a final page held by the buyer who purchased the capital itself, Lord Ambrose Vey. The beat is resolve hardening into plan.

chapters.title: An Invitation in Gilt
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Paloma infiltrates Vey's estate as a hired appraiser, discovering Vey's collection includes living citizens of Kestrel preserved as ornaments. The beat is cold fury beneath courtly manners.

chapters.title: The Ornament Garden
chapters.summary: Tam's POV. Tam finds his mother among Vey's preserved citizens — awake, aware, unable to move. The beat is heartbreak and the terrible question of whether restoration is mercy.

chapters.title: Terms of Surrender
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Caught by Vey, Paloma learns the truth of his own debt: the Guild bought his indenture with a page of Kestrel's name; he was collateral all along. The beat is betrayal reframing everything.

chapters.title: The Long Forgetting
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Imprisoned, Paloma begins reading the assembled pages to memorize the name, sacrificing memories one by one — first his childhood, then his mother's voice. The beat is elegiac self-erasure.

chapters.title: What Sefa Paid
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. Sefa, broken by Corvane, escapes with the location of the final page and dies delivering it, her last act restoring her daughter's name to her own memory. The beat is redemption at ruinous cost.

chapters.title: The Door Out of Kestrel
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Freed by Tam and the awakened garden-citizens, Paloma speaks the nearly complete name; a door opens onto a country suspended between existence and memory. The beat is awe — home as a threshold.

chapters.title: Corvane's Reckoning
chapters.summary: Climax begins. Paloma's POV. Corvane and Vey converge on the door to claim Kestrel whole; Paloma offers the trade the magic demands — one person must hold the entire country in memory, forever. The beat is the choice crystallizing.

chapters.title: The Inheritance
chapters.summary: Climax. Paloma's POV. Paloma takes the whole of Kestrel into himself — every street, every citizen including Tam's mother restored to the world — while his own past burns away. The beat is triumphant loss.

chapters.title: A Country That Remembers Him
chapters.summary: Falling action. Tam's POV. Kestrel stands again on the map; Tam, its returned citizen, cannot remember the scribe who saved him — only a warm absence shaped like a man. The beat is bittersweet gratitude.

chapters.title: Ledger of One
chapters.summary: Epilogue, Paloma's POV. Paloma walks the reborn Kestrel as a stranger with no name of his own, opening a new ledger whose first entry reads: 'Everything remembered. Nothing owed.' The beat is belonging found at the price of self — survival, finally paid in full.
